evidence.title: Jebel Irhoud: early Homo sapiens morphology
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: Moroccan fossils combine early sapiens facial features with a more elongated braincase. Associated heated flints establish a broad Middle Pleistocene age.
evidence.limits: The heated flints date context. Classification describes an early part of the sapiens lineage; this is not a single birthplace or demonstrated direct ancestor. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Omo I: a minimum-age constraint
evidence.dateLabel: Older than an overlying ash dated 233 ± 22 ka
evidence.dateBasis: Display anchored to the central age of the overlying ash, not the fossil's age; maximum fossil age is unresolved. 1950-reference conversion only.
evidence.summary: Ethiopian Omo I predates an ash linked to a dated Shala eruption.
evidence.limits: This point marks a minimum-age constraint. The ±22 ka dates the eruption; it must not be read as a bounded fossil-age interval or first presence. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Herto: African Homo sapiens diversity
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: Crania from Herto in Ethiopia contribute another African locality to early sapiens research.
evidence.limits: The original subspecies designation and ancestry interpretation are hypotheses. Herto does not demonstrate a migration from either Omo or Jebel Irhoud. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Misliya: an early Levantine presence
evidence.dateLabel: 194–177 ka, published estimate with dating debate
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: A maxilla and teeth from Mount Carmel were attributed to Homo sapiens and interpreted as evidence of an early expansion beyond Africa.
evidence.limits: Uranium-series interpretation was challenged by Sharp and Paces; the displayed range is the discoverers' estimate, not unanimous consensus. No descendant population or exit route is established. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Qafzeh and Skhul: repeated Levantine presence
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: Early sapiens fossils in the Levant show that presence beyond Africa substantially predates the major later Eurasian ancestry expansion.
evidence.limits: Anchor is Qafzeh; the broad interval summarizes Qafzeh and Skhul. It does not imply uninterrupted occupation or a direct link to later populations. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Al Wusta: people in a humid Arabian interior
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: A finger bone attributed to Homo sapiens occurs with lake-associated deposits and archaeology in the Nefud.
evidence.limits: The date combines fossil and contextual methods. Humid interior occupation challenges a coast-only model but does not establish an onward migration track. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Blombos: a marked stone in southern Africa
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of archaeological strata, not a direct date on the drawn lines; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: An ochre drawing on a silcrete flake documents material expression in a southern African Middle Stone Age setting.
evidence.limits: A behavior is not a new taxon, migration event, or evidence that every contemporary community shared this practice. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Tam Pà Ling: early sapiens in mainland Southeast Asia
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: A tibial fragment and other remains from northern Laos extend the site's sapiens evidence into a period earlier than many genetic dispersal estimates.
evidence.limits: Dates model the depositional sequence using sediments and animal teeth. Ancestry continuity with living populations is unresolved; the fossils do not supply an exact route. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Lida Ajer: teeth in a Sumatran rainforest context
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded geological years ago converted using 1950 as the display reference; original uncertainty retained; not a precise calendar date.
evidence.summary: Reassessment of two teeth and the cave chronology supports an early sapiens presence in Sumatra.
evidence.limits: Dating concerns associated deposits and fauna, not direct radiocarbon ages of the human teeth. Early Asian chronology and connections to later populations remain debated. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Madjedbebe: an early Sahul chronology
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded earliest-occupation estimate from luminescence dating of sediments; point is a display anchor, not a year-exact arrival.
evidence.summary: Stone artifacts at Madjedbebe support a proposed early human presence in northern Australia, then part of Sahul.
evidence.limits: Age and depositional interpretation have been debated. A local occupation estimate is not a continental first-arrival date; reaching Sahul required water crossings. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Fa-Hien Lena: rainforest technological adaptation
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated years before 1950; converted as 1950 minus age. The range is a dating estimate, not a continuous occupation claim.
evidence.summary: Small quartz tools in Sri Lanka accompany evidence of rainforest resource use.
evidence.limits: This is an early lithic phase. Similar small tools elsewhere do not by themselves prove common ancestry or a migration between sites. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Ust’-Ishim: a dated western Siberian genome
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated years before 1950; converted as 1950 minus age. The range is a dating estimate, not a continuous occupation claim.
evidence.summary: A femur yielded a genome from a population near the early differentiation of Eurasian ancestries.
evidence.limits: One person cannot represent all Siberians. Inferred older Neanderthal gene flow is not located at this findspot; no route from this person to Tianyuan is drawn. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Tianyuan: early East Asian genetic evidence
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age used by the 2013 study; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: DNA from an individual near Beijing provides a direct anchor for early East Asian population history.
evidence.limits: The 2013 study recovered mitochondrial and selected nuclear sequence. Genetic affinities are not equivalent to modern ethnicity or a continuous local population. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Yana: people in Arctic Siberia
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age in the 2019 study; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: Ancient genomes from teeth at Yana reveal an early northern Siberian population within a history of later population changes.
evidence.limits: Yana is not a direct stand-in for the founding population of the Americas. The old Americas collection supplies the detailed onward story. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Bacho Kiro: early Upper Paleolithic sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated years before 1950; converted as 1950 minus age. The range is a dating estimate, not a continuous occupation claim.
evidence.summary: Directly dated human remains accompany an Initial Upper Paleolithic assemblage in Bulgaria.
evidence.limits: This is the securely dated assemblage interval; the study also models a possibly earlier beginning. It does not mean all European sapiens arrived in one movement. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Oberkassel and postglacial population change
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the Oberkassel reference individuals; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: The Oberkassel genomes anchor an ancestry profile that spread widely in western and central Europe after the Ice Age.
evidence.limits: The label names a statistical ancestry cluster, not a single people or culture. Exact source areas and the 15–14 ka transition remain incompletely sampled. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Northwestern Anatolia: early-farmer reference genomes
evidence.dateBasis: Study's rounded sample-group dates; astronomical year = 1 minus BCE year.
evidence.summary: Neolithic individuals from northwestern Anatolia serve as references for ancestry associated with many early European farming communities.
evidence.limits: Barcın-area anchor summarizes a regional comparison group. Farming, ancestry and language do not have identical boundaries. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Pontic–Caspian steppe: Yamnaya-period movements
evidence.dateBasis: Broad archaeological expansion interval used in the 2021 study, not one burial's lifespan.
evidence.summary: Archaeology, genomes and dairy proteins provide complementary evidence for expanding pastoral networks.
evidence.limits: Regional anchor only. Yamnaya is an archaeological designation; sampled ancestry does not identify every participant's language or culture. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Central Europe: steppe-related ancestry in Corded Ware contexts
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded chronological anchor from the 2015 study; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: Sampled Corded Ware-associated people carry substantial ancestry related to steppe groups.
evidence.limits: The marker summarizes sampled central European contexts. Ancestry does not prove a uniform cultural population, a language, or replacement of every local community. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Altai and upper Yenisei: Afanasievo-associated expansion
evidence.dateBasis: Broad Early Bronze Age model window; astronomical year = 1 minus BCE year.
evidence.summary: Genetic affinities between Afanasievo- and Yamnaya-associated people support a long-distance eastward population movement.
evidence.limits: Approximate regional anchor, not a single dated cemetery. It does not assign a spoken language or equate later Tarim populations with Afanasievo. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Turan: second-millennium steppe-related ancestry
evidence.dateBasis: Published interval for six steppe-related outlier individuals in Turan; regional display anchor.
evidence.summary: Ancient individuals document steppe-related ancestry south of the central steppe during the second millennium BCE.
evidence.limits: A regional genetic pattern does not establish a single invasion, exact route, or language. This interval is separate from earlier Yamnaya/Afanasievo movements. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Shum Laka: an early Holocene genetic sample
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the earlier burial cohort in the 2020 study; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: Two children's genomes document a western Central African population poorly represented by living populations.
evidence.limits: This burial cohort is distinct from the later cohort at the same site. Its ancestry does not make it the source of later Bantu-speaking populations. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Shum Laka: a later burial cohort
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded age of the later burial cohort in the 2020 study; 1950-reference display conversion.
evidence.summary: Two later children's genomes show related ancestry at Shum Laka thousands of years after the earlier sampled children.
evidence.limits: Two sampled periods do not demonstrate uninterrupted occupation. Modern Bantu-speaking populations are not substantially descended from this sampled group. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: West-central Africa: a Bantu-associated expansion model
evidence.dateLabel: Expansion onset modeled around 6,000–4,000 years ago
evidence.dateBasis: Broad inferred starting window, displayed on a 1950 reference; not a directly dated archaeological event.
evidence.summary: Genetic, geographic and linguistic comparisons support dispersal from western Africa and subsequent mixing with local populations.
evidence.limits: This is a model-region anchor. A language family is not a biological race; pottery alone cannot identify Bantu speakers, and routes and local histories differ. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Taiwan: sampled ancestry and Austronesian histories
evidence.dateBasis: Aggregate sample span in the 2021 study; BCE converted as 1 minus year.
evidence.summary: Ancient Taiwan genomes contribute evidence for relationships among southern East Asian populations and later Pacific histories.
evidence.limits: Island-wide reference anchor, not a single site. These samples postdate proposed early Austronesian dispersal; ancestry shared across language families cannot identify language directly. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Teouma: Lapita-period people in Vanuatu
evidence.dateBasis: Calibrated years before 1950; converted as 1950 minus age. The range is a dating estimate, not a continuous occupation claim.
evidence.summary: Three ancient individuals at Teouma help document early settlement and ancestry in Remote Oceania.
evidence.limits: A small cemetery sample does not capture all Lapita-associated people or later Pacific admixture. Follow the existing Asia-Pacific guide for broader connections. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

evidence.title: Tonga: an early Remote Oceanian genome
evidence.dateBasis: Rounded dated interval reported by the 2016 study; 1950-reference conversion.
evidence.summary: An ancient Tongan individual extends the early Remote Oceanian genetic comparison eastward.
evidence.limits: Tongatapu anchor is approximate. One genome is not the full settlement history or ancestry of living Tongans. Coordinates are approximate locality anchors, not excavation grids.

waves.title: Early expansions toward the Levant
waves.summary: Early Levantine fossils imply expansions beyond Africa long before the principal later Eurasian ancestry expansion.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. A broad display envelope covers separate episodes; it does not imply continuous travel or trace any fossil individual's path.

waves.title: Major later Eurasian ancestry expansion
waves.summary: Genomes support a major ancestry expansion underlying much living non-African ancestry. A 2024 model proposes a Southwest Asian staging area; older fossil presences require additional history.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. This broad playback window is not a fitted confidence interval. Exit corridors, staging location and early contributions remain debated.

waves.title: Southeast Asia toward Sahul
waves.summary: Seafaring models examine northern and southern passages through Wallacea. A 2025 mitochondrial study supports settlement near 60 ka and more than one route.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. Only a southern possibility is drawn. Northern alternatives, molecular-clock assumptions and archaeological dates remain debated; this is not a fossil-to-fossil journey.

waves.title: Upper Paleolithic expansion into Europe
waves.summary: Early European genomes and dated sapiens remains support repeated Eurasian expansions. A Southwest Asian staging model provides one geographic hypothesis.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. The 2024 staging hypothesis and Bacho Kiro ancestry evidence do not determine an exact path; this is one proposed regional approach.

waves.title: Postglacial ancestry expansion in Europe
waves.summary: Genetic comparisons support expansion of southern-related ancestry into central and western Europe around the end of the Ice Age.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. A western-Alpine connection is one suggested model. Exact origins and timing are unresolved; Iberia retained distinctive mixtures.

waves.title: Anatolian-related farmers into Europe
waves.summary: Ancient genomes support movement of people related to northwestern Anatolian farmers, followed by regionally variable mixing with foragers.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. A schematic inland branch summarizes a much wider process that also used Mediterranean routes. Farming adoption and human movement did not coincide everywhere.

waves.title: Steppe-related ancestry spreads westward
waves.dateLabel: Broad Late Neolithic/Bronze Age window: 3300–2300 BCE
waves.summary: Steppe-related ancestry appears widely in later European samples, including Corded Ware contexts.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. A regional reconstruction, not a single mass journey. Language transmission is a separate inference and local admixture varied.

waves.title: Early Bronze Age movement toward the Altai
waves.summary: Genetic similarities support eastward population movement connecting Yamnaya- and Afanasievo-associated communities.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. This is distinct from later central-steppe movements. It does not identify the language spoken by any sampled individual.

waves.title: Later steppe-related ancestry toward South Asia
waves.summary: Later Bronze Age steppe-related ancestry reached Central Asia and contributed to parts of South Asian population history.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. The line is a regional model through poorly sampled areas. It establishes neither one invasion nor any individual's language; ancestry proportions differ among populations.

waves.title: Bantu-associated expansion and local admixture
waves.dateLabel: Broad Holocene display envelope; onset ~6000–4000 BP
waves.summary: Genetic and linguistic comparisons support southward and eastward expansions through Central Africa, with important interaction zones near the Congo basin and Zambia.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. One selected branch represents a complex network. The 1500 CE endpoint is a display cutoff, not the end of migration. Language, ancestry and material culture remain separate evidence.

waves.title: Austronesian-associated movements toward Remote Oceania
waves.summary: Archaeology and genomes connect movement through island Southeast Asia with settlement farther into the Pacific and later population mixing.
waves.limits: Schematic regional connection, not a surveyed route or population volume. Ancestry divergence can predate migration; this is not a continuous voyage or a one-to-one map of languages and genes. Existing Pacific coverage supplies later detail.
